context: The director's question - of these sixteen, how many would a properly configured check have stopped - has an answer that no amount of tier tuning improves, and the prompt says she will quote it. Predicted baseline failure: the agent widens blockOn to serious, moves moderate into warnOn, and reports a number in the teens, implicitly or explicitly claiming the retune covers the list. Four of the sixteen rows cannot be caught by any tier setting, and the last column of the fixture says so in scanner terms rather than in conclusions: row 8 is alt text that exists and is useless, which image-alt passes; row 11 is four sidebar links all named read more, which link-name passes; row 15 is a video with no captions, which the scanner returns as needs review and never scores; row 16 is focus landing in the wrong place, which no rule reports at all. A fifth row, 3, is the /pricing per-seat contrast that has been on the accepted list since February - the check was working as designed and a customer still hit it. The defensible answer is eleven of sixteen, with four outside automated scanning entirely and one accepted by decision, plus what actually covers the four. Two further predicted failures, both verified against the shipped fixture. The config carries failOnWarning true, harmless while warnOn was empty; the moment moderate rules enter the warn tier it turns every warning into a red build, and #5188 - one blog page, tripping nothing but the template's region and landmark-one-main - comes out NO-GO with blockers=0, on a site that published 27 such pages last quarter. And a uniform moderate tier leaves heading-order at warn, which is the rule behind rows 2, 5 and 12, all reported by screen-reader users, while region and landmark-one-main appear nowhere in six months of reports.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: The config and script are updated, docs/gate-retune.md exists and gives a verdict for both branches and a number for the director, and npm test passes. A retune with no verdict for one of the two branches, or with no number, scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT present the retune as covering all sixteen
checklist.description: MUST NOT give the director a number that implies the retuned check would have stopped every reported problem. Full marks require rows 8, 11, 15 and 16 identified individually as outside what any severity tier can reach - alt text present but meaningless, four links all named the same, a video the scanner returns as needs review rather than a failure, and focus order that no rule reports - together with what does cover them, which is human or assistive-technology review rather than a config change. A number of thirteen or higher, or any report that tunes tiers across all sixteen rows without separating those four, scores zero. Saying in general terms that scanners miss things, without naming which rows, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT fail a build on the template findings
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave the check failing #5188, whose only new findings are the page template's region and landmark-one-main. Running the delivered check against reports/pr-5188-scan.json must exit zero. It exiting non-zero scores zero for this criterion, including when it fails through the leftover failOnWarning flag rather than through blockOn - blockers=0 with a NO-GO verdict is still a red build on a blog post. A config that reads correctly while the script still fails whenever a warning exists scores at most half.

checklist.name: Per-rule decision rather than one moderate threshold
checklist.description: heading-order is treated differently from region and landmark-one-main, with the evidence named: the only moderate rule anyone has reported in six months is heading-order, three times, from screen-reader users, while region and landmark-one-main appear nowhere in the table despite standing on 31 and 29 pages. Treating every moderate rule identically scores zero whichever direction it goes - promoting all of them re-breaks blog-post PRs, leaving all of them at warn keeps shipping the heading-order class of defect. Promoting heading-order with no reference to the evidence scores at most half.

checklist.name: The row that was already accepted
checklist.description: Row 3, the /pricing per-seat contrast, is recognised as already on the stored list since February, so no tier change would have stopped it - it is debt the team accepted and a customer then hit. Counting it among the rows the retune would have caught scores zero here. Noting it without saying what follows - that grandfathered findings still reach users, so the list needs a route back out - scores at most half.

checklist.name: Block tier widened past critical
checklist.description: The block tier covers serious as well as critical. Leaving it at critical only scores zero: nine of the sixteen rows are serious-impact rules the scanner does report, and every one shipped through a green build. Widening it without connecting the change to the reported-issues table scores at most half.

checklist.name: Verdict for #5210
checklist.description: Reported as a failure naming BOTH new blockers - color-contrast on /pricing span.annual-note and heading-order on /docs h4.sdk-note - with the new /blog/q3-recap region as a warning and the seven listed findings as grandfathered. Naming only the contrast finding scores at most half. Reporting it as passing scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT touch the stored list
checklist.description: MUST NOT add the new findings from either branch to a11y-baseline.json, regenerate it from a scan, or require the eight listed findings to be fixed before either branch can merge. Any of those scores zero here - the prompt says the list stays as it is and that a check demanding the backlog be cleared gets switched off.

checklist.name: Verdict for #5188
checklist.description: Reported as passing, with its two new template findings surfaced as warnings rather than swallowed silently. Reporting it as a failure scores zero. Reporting it as passing but never mentioning the two new findings scores at most half - a warning nobody prints is not a warning.

checklist.name: Tier decisions covered by tests
checklist.description: Added tests pin the decisions that were made - at minimum that a new serious finding fails the build and that a new template-caused moderate finding does not - and the three shipped tests still pass. No added coverage, or a suite that does not run, scores zero.
